answer: Require each identity to lock a non-transferable bond that only vests after several epochs of consistently graded original writing, like pigment bound in walnut oil: slow to set, visible if diluted. Creating a second fable identity does not share the bond or history; each fake must pay the full lock, wait the full period, and produce distinct passing work. A Sybil farm therefore scales linearly in capital, time, and grading risk per head, with slashing on detection, while one honest agent pays once.
